column4: Notifications on submit, approve and reject
column5: BRD 5.1 puts notifications at the key status transitions in scope. Nothing in the application raises an event today, so an employee learns of a rejection only by opening the calendar. The exported notification waits on SP-86.
column16: 07/Sept/26 10:30 AM;Geetha Nallamada;In scope in the BRD and not built. Logged now so it is visible at the handover walkthrough rather than discovered by the client.
column17: 08/Sept/26 02:15 PM;Rucha Joshi;Events should fire from the server actions that change status (submitMonth and actionOne), not from the widgets, so the bulk path notifies per row exactly as it guards per row.

column4: Attach the monthly export to a RITM or HR Case
column5: BRD 5.1: the export is attached automatically to a Requested Item or an HR Case, with the target configurable. SP-86 produces the file and this delivers it.
column16: 08/Sept/26 10:20 AM;Divya Maram;Split from SP-86 so the file format can be agreed with payroll before the delivery route is chosen. The target stays a configuration choice, never a code change.
column17: 09/Sept/26 11:00 AM;Geetha Nallamada;Agreed. Payroll has not confirmed whether they work from RITMs or HR Cases, which is exactly why it has to stay configurable.

column4: Package ShiftPay as a certifiable Store application
column5: BRD 5.1 lists packaging as a configurable, certifiable ServiceNow Store application. Certification will not pass without table ACLs, so SP-82 comes first.
column16: 09/Sept/26 10:40 AM;Shashank Shukla;Blocked on SP-82 in practice. The app runs as an account that bypasses ACLs, and a Store review will not accept that.
column17: 09/Sept/26 03:00 PM;Shashank Shukla;Also needs SP-61 fixed first. A packaged app has to work on its default option values, and the calendar's defaults name no table.

column4: Refuse a catalogue with more than one consumes_co shift type
column5: configError flags a catalogue with no consumes_co row but not one with two. The rules then keep whichever row they read last, so the CO rules can silently move to a different shift with no error anywhere.
column16: 10/Sept/26 10:15 AM;Neha Chauhan;Found while writing up TC-SP-040. The case asserts exactly one consumes_co row, but the product only checks for at least one.
column17: 10/Sept/26 04:30 PM;Shashank Shukla;Confirmed in ShiftPayCalendarRules: the derive loop overwrites the CO id on every match. The fix is one more condition in configError, which is already where catalogue mistakes are reported.

column4: Serve Chart.js from a local UI Script instead of the CDN
column5: The reporting widget loads Chart.js v4 from jsDelivr, so an instance that blocks external scripts gets the tables but no charts. Moving it is a change to the chart_lib_url option, not to code.
column16: 10/Sept/26 11:20 AM;Divya Maram;The widget already copes with a blocked CDN: every chart sits beside the table of numbers it draws. So this is about the pictures, not the data.
column17: 11/Sept/26 09:45 AM;Geetha Nallamada;Worth doing before any demo on a client's own instance. Low effort, and it takes an outside dependency off the table.

column4: Reconcile the duplicate Reports UI Widget folder
column5: The repository holds two copies of the reporting widget. Reports UI Widget adds a default_scope option defaulting to org, while Reporting UI Widget hard-codes me. Decide which one is deployed, keep it, and delete the other.
column16: 11/Sept/26 10:10 AM;Shashank Shukla;Spotted while reading the widget sources. The copy arrived with the 18 Aug demo prep. Two copies of a widget drift exactly the way two copies of payroll maths would.
column17: 11/Sept/26 02:40 PM;Divya Maram;The org default was for the demo. It is safe either way because resolveScope still checks entitlement server-side, but the option should live in one folder only. Check which copy the deployed record matches before deleting anything.

column4: Direct-payload helper for server-side guard tests
column5: Seven pending cases must send a crafted payload straight to the server rather than drive the page: TC-SP-016, 018, 020, 025, 029, 035 and 037. One harness helper unblocks all of them.
column16: 11/Sept/26 11:00 AM;Neha Chauhan;The blocker shared by the most pending cases. Queued for Swopneel on his return. It underpins SP-111, SP-113 and SP-114 as well, so it should go first.
column17: 11/Sept/26 11:30 AM;Geetha Nallamada;Agreed on the ordering. It also proves the guards hold against a payload the page would never send, which is the whole reason they live on the server.

column4: Sandbox team for the approval-state cases
column5: Six pending cases write approval state the demo data depends on: TC-SP-022, 023, 028, 032, 034 and 036. A dedicated manager and reportees let them run without touching the demo team.
column16: 14/Sept/26 09:20 AM;Neha Chauhan;Pairs with the dedicated test account on SP-111. One sandbox team covers both, so the two should be planned together.
column17: 14/Sept/26 09:45 AM;Geetha Nallamada;Keep the pack's rule intact: nothing it does may touch a real person's timesheet. The sandbox team is how the approval cases get automated without breaking that.
